text:
Nisha: heads-up: saw a TP all-reduce tail on dev nodes this morning — latency spikes when kv-cache hit-rate jumps during inference (TP=4).

James: reproable locally or only on dev cluster?

Nisha: repro on dev (A100x8), also faintly on my laptop when I force kv cache behavior. quick paste of the perf snip:
```
[2026-03-17 09:12:34] step=1203 tp=4 pp=1 msg_size=512B tokens=64 allreduce_total=21.1ms allreduce_wait=15.6ms compute=4.8ms kv_hit_rate=0.83 batch=1
[2026-03-17 09:12:35] step=1204 tp=4 pp=1 msg_size=2048B allreduce_total=9.2ms allreduce_wait=1.1ms compute=7.5ms kv_hit_rate=0.12 batch=1
```

Kai: interesting — msg_size=512 shows large wait. did kernel selection pick tree or ring for that size?

Nisha: runtime logs show it picked tree fallback for <1KB per-chunk. suspicion: fragmentation + kvcache eviction pattern creates a flurry of many small allreduces that favor tree but suffer from serialization.

Maria: tree has lower latency for tiny msgs usually, but with TP pipeline overlap and many simultaneous micro-allreduces tree rendezvous can serialize because of extra synchronization steps.

James: any NCCL tuning flags set? NCCL_ALGO, COLL_NET, or something aggressive?

Nisha: using defaults plus NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME set. tried NCCL_ALGO=tree locally — actually made the tail worse. ring seemed better for these bursts.

Kai: can you share the bash command to reproduce? I'll run a quick sweep with nccl-tests and our microbench harness.

Nisha: repro command I ran:
```
./bench_tp --tp 4 --pp 1 --model tiny --kvpattern=hotburst --batch=1 --max-toks=64 --msg-algo=auto
```
and a direct nccl test to emulate many small reduces:
```
./nccl-tests/all_reduce_perf -b 512 -e 512 -f 2 -g 4
```

Maria: try forcing ring vs tree in the runtime to compare. also add kernel selection logging and the chosen kernel id + estimated latency to trace. we need a perf profile across msg_size distribution.

James: agreed. I'll instrument: log {kernel_id, msg_size, predicted_ms, observed_ms, kv_hit_rate} and add p95/p99 counters.

Kai: hypothesis: the runtime's kernel selector uses a static threshold around 1KB that doesn't account for burstiness and KV cache pressure. When kvcache hits spike, compute goes down and network wait dominates, shifting the optimal kernel toward ring for pipelined overlap.

Nisha: yep. reproduced with a synthetic pattern that toggles kvcache: hotburst generator attached.

infra-bot: job 4521 finished: bench_tp hotburst sweep (tp=4) — artifacts uploaded to gs://redwood-perf/4521/

Maria: nice. next steps:
- James to add kernel-selection trace and p99 counters (ETA today)
- Kai to run ring/tree sweep across msg sizes [128,256,512,1024,2048] with kvcache hotburst pattern (ETA EOD)
- Nisha to add microbench harness to emulate kv eviction spikes and confirm regression window

James: also adding an AB test: if predicted_allreduce_ms deviates from observed by >20% switch to alternative kernel for next 100ms (trial window). Might mitigate tail while we tune thresholds.

Nisha: can we also test batching heuristics? batching small requests can change per-chunk msg size distribution. I suspect current batching groups keep small chunk sizes and make many tiny allreduces instead of a few larger ones.

Kai: good call — I'll measure effective per-gpu message size and look at batching config: target_seq_len, max_batch_bytes, and coalescing window.

Maria: if experiments show ring outperforms in these bursts, we should update kernel selector to use dynamic policy: prefer ring when kv_hit_rate>0.7 and predicted_net_wait > predicted_compute*2 (or some tunable heuristic).

James: logging patch pushed to perf branch: https://git.internal/redwood/rt-perf/compare/infra-kerneltrace

Nisha: thanks all. saving artifacts and a short repro script to the perf bucket. I'll paste link in #eng-runtime once done. :eyes: 

Maria: filing a short incident note and linking experiments so CS teams know if they see similar client reports.

Nisha: last note — this only affected TP full-parallel runs (tp>1). single-GPU runs fine. makes sense given multi-stage allreduce scatter pattern.

Kai: running sweep now.

(threads will follow with logs and small diffs)
